version.changelog:
huo15-img-prompt v2.3.0 introduces major upgrades to T2I/T2V prompt generation, now as a comprehensive six-tool suite.

- Added Claude API-powered intelligent prompt polishing for enhanced professionalism and style.
- Introduced platform compliance rewriting: detects high-risk phrases for SD/MJ/DALL-E and suggests legal artistic alternatives.
- Improved video prompting: supports 9 video models, 30 camera motions, and 3-stage keyframes.
- Enhanced image prompt features: 88 style presets, mixed-style control, and five-fold consistency (character, style, camera, lighting, palette).
- Expanded preset and auto-detection support for more artistic and video generation scenarios.
- Now supports direct image output (ComfyUI, SD-WebUI, DALL-E) and reverse image-prompt extraction for A1111, ComfyUI, and NovelAI user metadata.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: huo15-img-prompt
Version: 2.3.0

The huo15-img-prompt skill bundle is a comprehensive and well-documented toolset for AI image and video prompt engineering. It provides scripts for prompt enhancement (enhance_prompt.py), video-specific prompting (enhance_video.py), image metadata extraction (reverse_prompt.py), and direct rendering via external APIs (render_prompt.py). It also includes advanced features like LLM-based polishing (claude_polish.py) and a robust safety filter (safety_lint.py) designed to prevent the generation of harmful content while allowing legitimate artistic expression. While the scripts utilize network access and sensitive environment variables (e.g., ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY), these behaviors are strictly aligned with the stated purpose of interacting with AI services. The code is transparent, avoids unnecessary third-party dependencies, and shows no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized execution.

llm.summary: The skill largely does what it claims (prompt enhancement, optional Claude polishing, safety-linting, and optional direct rendering), but the package metadata omits required environment variables and the runtime can send user content to external APIs — the discrepancy and network behavior warrant caution before installing or giving API keys.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (prompt enhancement, Claude polish, safety lint, video support, and direct rendering) matches the shipped scripts: enhance_prompt.py, enhance_video.py, reverse_prompt.py, render_prompt.py, claude_polish.py, safety_lint.py. However the registry lists no required environment variables while code clearly supports/needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (claude_polish) and OPENAI_API_KEY (rendering via DALL‑E) and accepts COMFYUI_URL/SDWEBUI_URL — the metadata omission is inconsistent and could mislead users about what credentials will be used.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run the included scripts (enhance_prompt.py, etc.) and examples show automatic agent invocation on trigger words. The scripts perform local prompt construction and also make outbound HTTP calls to Anthropic/OpenAI/local ComfyUI/SDWebUI endpoints. That behavior is coherent with the described features, but using flags like --polish or --backend=dalle will transmit user-provided prompts (and possibly metadata) to third-party services. reverse_prompt.py supports remote URLs and a VLM fallback which may call external VLM/model APIs. The SKILL.md does not explicitly warn that user data will be sent externally when certain options are used.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only style with bundled scripts). That is low risk from an installer perspective — nothing is downloaded at install time. The shipped code itself will execute when invoked.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The code expects and uses sensitive environment variables (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY) and supports overriding local endpoints (COMFYUI_URL, SDWEBUI_URL), but the registry's required env vars list is empty. The credentials requested by the code are proportionate to the optional features (Claude polish and DALL‑E rendering), however the metadata omission is misleading and could cause users to inadvertently provide keys without realizing which scripts consume them. safety_lint claims to be local-only (no network) which matches the changelog, but the tool also provides transformations intended to avoid platform rejections — this could be misused to try to evade moderation if abused.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request permanent platform-wide privileges. The scripts operate on demand and do not modify other skills or system-wide agent configuration in the provided code.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package contains useful prompt-engineering tools and direct-render helpers, but note two practical risks: (1) the code will call external services when you use certain flags — claude_polish.py requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and render_prompt.py will use OPENAI_API_KEY for DALL‑E (and both use plain HTTP requests). Those env vars are not declared in the registry metadata, so double-check before supplying API keys. (2) reverse_prompt and VLM fallback may transmit image URLs or extracted metadata to external model APIs. Before installing: review the code paths that call urlopen (claude_polish.py, render_prompt.py, reverse_prompt.py) to confirm what data is sent; prefer running in an isolated environment; only provide API keys with least privilege and test with non-sensitive inputs. If you rely on local backends (ComfyUI/SD WebUI), ensure they are running locally and network-exposed URLs are correct. Finally, be cautious about the safety_lint transformations — they are intended to make prompts compliant, but consider auditing examples to ensure they won't be misused to evade content moderation.
